messages.subject: Problem of installing rhipe
messages.body_plain:
Hi there, I've tried to install rhipe but got the following error
message:
-------
cls3415@ubuntu:~/Downloads$ sudo R CMD INSTALL Rhipe_0.60.tar.gz *
installing to library ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library’
* installing *source* package ‘Rhipe’ ...
checking for gcc... gcc -std=gnu99
checking for C compiler default output file name... rm: cannot remove
`a.out.dSYM': Is a directory
a.out
checking whether the C compiler works... yes
checking whether we are cross compiling... no
checking for suffix of executables...
checking for suffix of object files... o
checking whether we are using the GNU C compiler... yes
checking whether gcc -std=gnu99 accepts -g... yes
checking for gcc -std=gnu99 option to accept ISO C89... none needed
configure: creating ./config.status
config.status: creating src/Makevars
** libs
g++ -I/usr/share/R/include      -fpic  -g -O2 -I. -g  -
DHAVE_UINTPTR_T  `pkg-config --cflags protobuf` -Wall -c display.cc -o
display.o
In file included from ream.h:9,
                 from display.cc:1:
./rexp.pb.h:12:2: error: #error This file was generated by a newer
version of protoc which is
./rexp.pb.h:13:2: error: #error incompatible with your Protocol Buffer
headers. Please update
./rexp.pb.h:14:2: error: #error your headers.
display.cc: In function ‘SEXPREC* collect_buffer(SEXPREC*, SEXPREC*)’:
display.cc:247: warning: deprecated conversion from string constant to
‘char*’
display.cc:247: warning: deprecated conversion from string constant to
‘char*’
display.cc: In function ‘int32_t readJavaInt(FILE*)’:
display.cc:349: warning: ignoring return value of ‘size_t fread(void*,
size_t, size_t, FILE*)’, declared with attribute warn_unused_result
make: *** [display.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘Rhipe’
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe’
---------------------
Could anyone tell me how to install rhipe correctly??

Thanks.
S.H.

messages.body_plain:
> I unzipped the file I downloaded from http://code.google.com/p/protobuf/downloads/detail?name=protobuf-2.3.0.tar.bz2&can=2&q=, and then type "sh configure".

You did type:(?)

 make && make install
# you might need to run sudo make install (assuming you have root permissions)

If you have already done so, try running this

pkg-config --modversion protobuf

and report the output.

It is possible that the protobuf 2.3 was not installed in the same place(as the old one) and okg-config picks up the old version.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Problem of installing rhipe
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Sure. There are 3 approaches

1) Install protobuf into /usr/lib and /usr/include i.e. run ./configure --prefix=/usr && make && make install
    I do not prefer this since protobuf is not system specific, rather an add on(like an application) and really should go to /usr/local

2) In the bash profile oyu need
EXPORT LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/to/path1:/to/path2:/where/to/path3

but this needs to be done for every user or (assuming you're sysadmin) you can just modify /etc/profile (again this works if everyone uses bash)

See http://www.network-theory.co.uk/docs/gccintro/gccintro_25.html , specifically
"It is possible for the system administrator to set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH variable for all users, by adding it to a default login script, such as ‘/etc/profile’. "

3) Modify or place an entry in /etc/ld.so.conf.d/ or /etc/ld.so.conf (to include /usr/local/lib  - i.e the place where protobuf installs its libs)
And then update the cache, by ldconfig
(see man ld.so and man ldconfig)

Finally, to confirm all is indeed okay, do the ldd once again.

Hope it helps
Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
You're almost there. You need to set the environment variable HADOOP to the folder containing the bin folder that contains the hadoop shell file.
For example if hadoop is installed in /a/hadoop-2/ ( so that /a/hadoop-2/bin contains the hadoop shell file) then set HADOOP to /a/hadoop-2/ . On cloudera I /think/you can set HADOOP to / .
Do this in your bash profile or .bashrc .
You can also do

HADOOP=path R CMD INSTALL ....

To install. But library(Rhipe) will fail, for that set the environment variables ( which you could do with Sys.setenv)

Saptarshi

But did you reload .bashrc ? Confirm that indeed HADOOP is present.
Before R CMD INSTALL

$HADOOP

should be /usr/lib/hadoop

and you need export HADOOP=/usr/lib/hadoop , without the export it won't be visible to other processes.

Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Problem of installing rhipe
messages.body_plain:
You setting the environment variable as yourself, but installing RHIPE as root.
The new variable is not transferred over.

E.g.
echo 'print(Sys.getenv("HADOOP"))' > a.r

R CMD BATCH a.r
cat a.r.Rout

sudo R CMD BATCH a.r
cat a.r.Rout

note the difference.

So, what you can do
a) modify the /etc/bashrc and see that everyones bashrc sources this.

or
(b) su root and do the rest

Not sure which is better.
Regards
Saptarshi

messages.body_snippet:
You setting the environment variable as yourself, but installing RHIPE as root.
The new variable is not transferred over.

E.g.
echo 'print(Sys.getenv("HADOOP"))' > a.r

R CMD BATCH a.r
cat a.r.Rout

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Problem in simple example from http://www.stat.purdue.edu/~sguha/rhipe/doc/html/examples.html
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Saptarshi!!!
I've tried (a), but it just kept running w/o stopping.
So, I tried (b). I save the script in Rscript.sh with
-----------------------
export R_HOME=/usr/lib/R
/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe/libs/imperious.so
----------------------
which I checked from R shell by using commands you showed me.
But when I sh Rscript.sh, it shows
--------------
Rscript.sh: 3: io.sort.mb=1: not found
/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe/libs/imperious.so: error while loading shared libraries: libR.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
--------------

I'm using hadoop-conf-pseudo mode in a VMware.
Is that the reason caused these problem? I mean from problem of install to run the example.
Thanks!!!

S.H.
--------------

messages.subject: Parallelize statistical models/algorithms
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Would like any information on the following topics:

-> How do I run advanced statistical techniques such as linear
regression , logistic, K-means on a cluster using rhipe
-> Methodology to apply to parallelize these procedures.
-> Any libraries available already which gives us Map-Reduce versions
of existing R libraries
-> Something similiar to Apache Mahout (http://mahout.apache.org/) in
R ?

Thanks in advance,

Deepak

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Parallelize statistical models/algorithms
messages.body_plain:
H Deepak,

I haven't attempted implementing all sorts of algorithms using RHIPE.
Primarily use it to store data and analyze by smaller subsets, recombining the results.
However

> -> How do I run advanced statistical techniques such as linear
> regression , logistic, K-means on a cluster using rhipe

k-means is straightforward. See the mahout page for their approach,
you'll do something similar in RHIPE. The code will be quite short.
Others, haven't thought of.

> -> Methodology to apply to parallelize these procedures.

> -> Any libraries available already which gives us Map-Reduce versions
> of existing R libraries

None that I've heard of.

> -> Something similiar to Apache Mahout (http://mahout.apache.org/) in
> R ?
>

Haven't heard of any of these. Meanwhile, I'm planning on writing matrix addition/multiplication
routines, which will in be java but can be called from R.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Integrating with HDF5
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I do not have much experienced with R but have been working with
Hadoop over the past few months.  One of the key items we are looking
at is the use of HDF5 with Hadoop.  I know that R can interact with
HDF5 files and was wondering if anyone has any experience using the
three together (R, HDF5, Hadoop).

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Integrating with HDF5
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
This indeed looks very possible. What is required is an InputFormat, which also should include a RecordReader. The record reader should emit key,values that are RHByteWritable classes.
Essentially, a way to split the file across key,values independently. I think HDF5 has a header/dictionary that assists in this.

Anyone out there familiar with HDF5 and InputFormats?

Regards
Saptarshi
